transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-22
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: ~47 min
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Morris (Redwood SE), Marcus Liu (Horizon AI CTO), Priya Kapoor (Head of ML), David Chen (Infra), Anika Rao (PM)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on model selection, context length needs (40k+), multilingual support, and tool-calling/function-calling requirements; discuss Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and run initial benchmarks. Ended with clear next steps to share pricing and eval harness.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, im joined by Elena on the call, hows it going
[00:00:07] Marcus: good, thanks — sorry sneaking in from a cafe so you might hear background — Marcus here CTO at Horizon
[00:00:12] Elena: hi Marcus, Priya, David, Anika — Elena from Redwood, I handle solutions and benchmarks
[00:00:18] Priya: hey all, Priya here, super excited, we wanted to use this time to validate model choices and understand the deployment modes — hosted, dedicated, private — and what fits our compliance and latency needs
[00:00:30] Jordan: perfect. quick go-around: can you remind us of current stack, infra, and what success looks like?
[00:00:38] Marcus: sure. Horizon runs most inference on GCP, using k8s for microservices, we have gpu instances for training but currently use OpenAI for a few prod endpoints. main constraints: PII staying in region, we need SAML + SSO for org, and prefer keystore integration — we use Google KMS. latency target for interactive features is p95 < 300ms for short chats, and for long form summarization throughput matter more. Also we're exploring 100k token like long context for doc summarization — is that realistic?
[00:01:12] Elena: yeah, thanks. Redwood supports model variants that hit different context windows; for 100k though usually you look at a mixture of chunking plus a long-context model, or a model with extended position embeddings. We can demo both. one thing to flag: the runtime can do prefix/KV cache to reduce cost on repeated contexts but sometimes the transcript tool mislabels KV as 'K V cash' in our logs (laughs) — just so you know the naming might be a little off in transcripts
[00:01:40] David: that's helpful. For compliance we need audit logs, and also want to know if private deployment can be air-gapped.
[00:01:47] Jordan: yes, Private (on-prem) can be air-gapped; Redwood Private offers a customer-managed control plane and we can plug into your KMS/HSM. we've done SOC2/ISO customers; we'll share the security pack.
[00:01:58] Priya: great. on the models side, we're weighing open models — are we talking Llama derivatives, Mistral, open-instruct, and also the Anthropic family? we need multilingual (EN, ES, FR, ZH) with low hallucination on domain-specific terms.
[00:02:14] Elena: right. typical comps are Llama-2 variants, Mistral x, Mistral-instruct, and we see some customers evaluate LlamaX style models and dedicated Anthropic for safety. Redwood keeps a model catalog and we run perf/quality profiles — we can share side-by-side evals for your prompt set. note: some names get transcribed odd in meetings so the catalog ID is the source of truth.
[00:02:34] Marcus: for cost, how do hosted vs dedicated differ? if we have sustained 3k reqs/min, is dedicated a must?
[00:02:42] Jordan: dedicated is for predictable throughput and isolation; committed capacity reduces unit price. hosted is easier to start and has burst, but you trade-off predictability and some control over network. for 3k rps sustained you'd likely look at reserved dedicated pools or a hybrid model — we can run capacity planning with Elena's benchmarks.
[00:03:00] Anika: timeline wise, we want a pilot in Q3, maybe start a POC in 6 weeks, target production by end of Q3.
[00:03:06] Jordan: sounds reasonable.
[00:03:08] Elena: quick technical: tool-calling / function-calling — we support structured tool calling (webhook style and typed outputs). you mentioned needing db lookups, internal API calls, and RAG pipelines?
[00:03:20] Priya: yep, RAG + tool calling to fetch user profile data prefilled in prompts. and we want deterministic outputs for some flows so ability to pin model versions is important.
[00:03:30] Elena: Redwood supports model pinning and rollout strategies (canary, A/B). for deterministic flows you might tune sampling params or use smaller models. also we have structured output helpers so you can return JSON that maps directly to downstream services.
[00:03:43] Marcus: about multilingual — how is tokenization and cost tracked? some of our languages blow up token counts which affects cost.
[00:03:50] Jordan: good point. our console shows token breakdown by language and model; we can show a sample where Spanish/Chinese tokenization differs. Elena, we have a quick sim?
[00:03:58] Elena: yes, I can run a short script but offline; for now, typical guidance: use the model that matches language needs, and we can quantize where needed to cut costs. our Optimize product suggests model+quantization combos per workload.
[00:04:12] David: security follow-ups: do you support SSO via SAML/OIDC and per-route RBAC? we need zone-restricted endpoints for EU data residency.
[00:04:20] Jordan: yes SAML and OIDC, per-route RBAC, and routing by region is supported. Private gives you the most control for residency.
[00:04:27] Priya: can we run a stress test that includes both short chat latency and long-context summarization? want to see end-to-end including network and KV cache behavior.
[00:04:35] Elena: absolutely. typical plan: we run a 48-hour benchmark with your prompts, mixing 2k short chats and 500 long-doc summarizations to map p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens. we'll also test model fallback behavior.
[00:04:49] Marcus: about model fallbacks — if host capacity is constrained will requests reroute to smaller model variants? what about output quality regressions?
[00:04:56] Jordan: yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible variants; Redwood console gives quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to evals and prompt sets so you can be notified if fallback degrades outputs. you can also set hard rules to avoid fallback for critical flows.
[00:05:10] Anika: contract mechanics — is billing usage-based for hosted and commit for dedicated? can we mix?
[00:05:15] Jordan: hosted is usage-based; dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. hybrid is possible — you can keep burst on hosted and reserve base capacity.
[00:05:23] Priya: one more on tool-calling: we want typed responses that our orchestration layer can consume; any examples?
[00:05:29] Elena: yes, we have function-calling examples where the LLM returns strict JSON and Redwood runtime validates and routes to your webhook. I will share a short example in the eval harness.
[00:05:38] Marcus: ok sounds good. any limitations on model size for private on-prem? we have A100s with multi-GPU nodes and want low-latency 16ms per token for small inference — probably unrealistic but curious.
[00:05:49] Elena: small token latencies like 16ms depend on model, batch size, and kernel optimizations. our serving runtime picks kernels per topology and can hit single-digit ms for tiny models; for large 70B+ models latency will be higher but we can use quantization and CPU offload for cost tradeoffs. we'll capture realistic expectations in the benchmark report.
[00:06:06] Jordan: want to capture some nonfunctional requirements now — Marcus can you list top 3?
[00:06:11] Marcus: sure: 1) data residency EU for certain products, 2) audit log retention 1 year, 3) p95 chat latency <300ms.
[00:06:20] Jordan: noted.
[00:06:22] Priya: for evaluation, what's the simplest path to prove model quality on our domain?
[00:06:26] Elena: share representative prompts and a labeled eval set if you have it. we run automatic pass/fail metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-ish, but also domain-specific checks), plus human checks for hallucination. we can include multilingual metrics per language.
[00:06:40] David: is there an opinionated prompt engineering guide from Redwood for best results?
[00:06:44] Jordan: yes we have a docs section and an example prompt pack — I'll include that link.
[00:06:48] Anika: any legal red flags for us needing to involve procurement?
[00:06:52] Jordan: standard enterprise contract flow — we'll send an initial SOW and security pack; procurement usually loops in after the POC approval.
[00:06:58] Priya: ok great. can we see a concrete timeline of next steps right now?
[00:07:02] Jordan: sure — immediate: Jordan sends pricing and SLA; Elena shares harness and sample scripts; customer shares prompts and compliance doc; then week of 5/28 do live benchmark deep-dive.
[00:07:14] Marcus: acceptable.
[00:07:17] Elena: quick aside — for long-context workflows some customers do a hybrid RAG where they chunk and store embeddings, but the runtime's KV/prefix cache can also keep active session context to reduce recomputation. sometimes the transcription will write 'KV cash' but we mean KV cache — yep that happens a lot in real calls.
[00:07:36] Jordan: (laughs) noted. any final questions?
[00:07:40] Priya: one: do you support deterministic tokenization for exact-match legal text extraction?
[00:07:45] Elena: we can configure tokenizers and provide deterministic sampling settings; for legal extraction we usually recommend a smaller model with constrained decoding and multiple verification passes.
[00:07:56] Marcus: ok thanks thats enough for now. we'll get the prompt sets over this week.
[00:08:01] Jordan: awesome, we'll follow up with the artifacts. thanks everyone.
[00:08:05] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains some mis-transcriptions and shorthand; audio quality ok but occasional background noise from one participant. Follow-up items captured in action_items and next_steps above.
